summary:
Pakal-Sat: Eyes on Earth, Mind on the Stars is a dynamic digital platform designed to interact with analog sites located across the planet. By comparing environments, landforms, climates, ecosystems, and vegetation from various regions—using data compiled from NASA databases—the platform identifies geographic locations that share key characteristics with the Moon and Mars. These sites can serve as future testing grounds for new exploration equipment, landing simulations, and the establishment of permanent bases.
In this way, the project aims to support the preparation of future space missions to these destinations, fostering the development of the knowledge, technologies, and capabilities necessary for humans to adapt to new environments—all by exploring and utilizing analog settings found here on Earth.
details:
What exactly does it do?

Pakal-Sat is an interactive digital platform that aims to identify places on Earth with characteristics similar to those of the Moon and Mars by comparing their topography, climate, terrain, geology, and vegetation.

How does it work?

It uses satellite information and NASA databases to analyze and compare different regions on Earth with the surfaces of the Moon and Mars. Through maps and visualizations, it helps identify potential locations for space exploration experiments.

What are its benefits?

  • It helps identify terrains similar to those on the Moon and Mars.
  • It helps reduce costs and risks in future space missions.
  • It allows researchers to evaluate locations for testing robots, vehicles, and exploration equipment.
  • It uses available scientific information to support new research.

What do we hope to achieve?

We aim to identify new strategic locations on Earth that could be used as testing and simulation sites for space exploration, contributing to the development of new technologies and the preparation of future missions to the Moon and Mars.
